passages.note: Wesco is listed as House sponsor of SB 101, whose digest describes the compelling-interest/least-restrictive-means exemption test.
Wesco, named as the bill's House sponsor, voted Yea on SB 101's single-subject third reading, 63-31.

passages.provision_quote: Sec. 8. (a) Except as provided in subsection (b), a governmental entity may not substantially burden a person's exercise of religion, SEA 101 — Concur 3 even if the burden results from a rule of general applicability. (b) A governmental entity may substantially burden a person's exercise of religion only if the governmental entity demonstrates that application of the burden to the person: (1) is in furtherance of a compelling governmental interest; and (2) is the least restrictive means of furthering that compelling governmental interest.
passages.note: Sec. 8 states the compelling-interest/least-restrictive-means test that limits the exemption, the RFRA pattern the annex rules to rung 4.

rows.reasoning: Wesco sponsored and voted Yea for SB 101 (2015), Indiana's Religious Freedom Restoration Act, which bars government from substantially burdening a person's exercise of religion unless it proves the burden furthers a compelling governmental interest by the least restrictive means. Per the annex's ruled reading, a RFRA of this shape matches rung 4, "protect religious freedom and allow faith-based exemptions from laws that conflict with sincere religious beliefs," because the exemption is the default and the compelling-interest test only limits it.
